existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Patient has one hard local R4-to-R6 validation break (`Patient.communication.language` binding is now required), plus material contact-model migration risks. The top concerns are stricter language coding, separating contact personal relationship from functional role, and preserving R6-only contact extra names/addresses when exchanging with R4. The biggest uncertainty is terminology mapping for the contact relationship split.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should normalize `Patient.communication.language` to BCP-47 codings, explicitly map contact relationship codes into R6 `relationship` versus `role`, and define a preservation strategy for R6 `additionalName` and `additionalAddress` when producing R4. Existing R4 instances are otherwise structurally stable: no local Patient elements were removed, local cardinalities and reference targets are unchanged, and choice type sets did not narrow.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable Patient StructureDefinition deltas because both assigned StructureDefinitions and package indexes were present. Confidence is medium for exact terminology migration guidance around contact roles because no terminology expansion, official diff, narrative page, or ConceptMap was available, and the R6 package lacks a local copy of the external v3 personal-relationship value set.

rationaleMd:

R4 maturity context is normative/FMM 5, which creates strong stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 42/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

10 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Because R4 stability pressure is strong, low-cost compatible designs should be preferred unless they clearly undermine the R6 goal.
